item.title: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian says he is open to allowing nuclear inspectors into country
item.description: In an interview with "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" on Friday, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said that he is open to allowing international nuclear inspectors into Iran but not under the "existing framework" set up since the U.S. withdrew from the 2015 nuclear deal.

item.title: Sylvester Stallone on the fight to make "Rocky"
item.description: Sylvester Stallone was a struggling actor who wrote the perfect script for himself – and refused to sell it unless he played the title role. He talks about his new memoir, "The Steps," that recounts his rocky road to fame before and after "Rocky."

item.title: Extended interview: Sylvester Stallone
item.description: In this web exclusive, actor, writer and director Sylvester Stallone talks with correspondent Tracy Smith about his career, including his first experience as an actor in a school production of "Death of a Salesman"; how rejection made him tougher; why he refused to sell his screenplay for "Rocky" unless he played the lead role; and how he continued to fight during the film's production to maintain his vision of the character.

item.title: Sylvester Stallone on the fight to make "Rocky"
item.description: He was a struggling actor who created his own big break by writing the perfect screenplay for himself – and refusing to sell it without being given the starring role. Sylvester Stallone talks with correspondent Tracy Smith about his new memoir, "The Steps," that recounts his rocky road to fame before and after "Rocky."

item.title: True crime, where there's nothing hotter than a cold case
item.description: Today the public's appetite for true crime – from TV shows and podcasts to the big screen – has never been bigger, as devotees of the genre even spend their time trying to solve crimes. Correspondent Luke Burbank visits the annual CrimeCon convention, and talks with Karen Kilgariff and Georgia Hardstark, hosts of the "My Favorite Murder" podcast, and professor Jean Murley, about the appeal of crime as entertainment.
